date_note: Cyber Kendra's page is dated Nov 20 but states the situation as of Nov 19; published date taken as Nov 19.
title: FastUnlock: unpatched Windows 11 Narrator flaw lets an attacker with physical access bypass the lock screen and BitLocker, researcher claims
summary: A researcher using the names Chaotic Eclipse and Nightmare-Eclipse posted 'FastUnlock' files on GitHub without coordinating with Microsoft. They claim a Narrator lock-screen flaw lets someone with physical access run code and get into a BitLocker-encrypted Windows 11 26H2 machine in about five minutes, and say it needs at least one account linked to a Microsoft account. It has no CVE and Microsoft has published no advisory; Cyber Kendra did not reproduce it.
plain: A researcher says a lost or stolen Windows 11 laptop could be unlocked using the screen reader feature. Microsoft has not responded and there is no fix.
exec: Matters for lost or stolen laptops that rely on BitLocker; physical access is required and no attacks in the wild are reported.
action: Until Microsoft responds, consider blocking Narrator on the lock screen with AppLocker or a restrictive DACL (the researcher's suggestion; test first) and keep devices physically secured.

key_findings: No CVE as of Nov 19; no Microsoft advisory, fix or workaround listed.
Needs physical access and a local account linked to a Microsoft account.
Researcher suggests blocking Narrator via AppLocker or a custom DACL as a possible fix.
recommendations: Secure devices physically; consider blocking Narrator until a patch ships.

validation.note: Cyber Kendra and Security Affairs (19 Nov) both relay the researcher's own advisory; neither reproduced it or reports a Microsoft response or CVE. Security Affairs says the researcher tested Windows 11 26H2 with the November updates and has not checked Windows 10. GitHub advisory not opened. Not independent confirmation, so it stays an unconfirmed claim.

review.note: Compared title, claimed status, severity 1, date, Windows 11 26H2, five minutes, Microsoft-account precondition, no CVE or advisory, AppLocker/DACL suggestion against Cyber Kendra and Security Affairs; neither reproduced
